item: The product is three programs: a Rust shell, a React UI and a Bun sidecar that talks to the UI through the shell.
The UI owns the database and runs git; the sidecar and the Rust shell do neither.
One agent process per active chat, started and supervised by the sidecar.
The Rust shell provides window, menus, notifications, updater, terminals and database migrations to the UI.
Tauri plugin set: shell, sql, fs, dialog, notification, clipboard, deep-link, opener and window-state exist; http, store and updater plugins are not registered yet.
Small UI state kept in local-storage JSON files per subsystem; ours lists each file store with its lifetime and has no shared layer.
The sidecar ships as one compiled Bun executable, started in a mode chosen by argument; --version and the Tauri externalBin wiring are not built.
The sidecar bundles the Claude Agent SDK.
Codex is driven through codex app-server over JSON-RPC.
An ACP client drives OpenCode, Pi and similar agents.
Zod validates every RPC message in both directions.
The sidecar logs through its own Logger interface instead of pino.
The sidecar listens on a Unix socket only, with no HTTP server and no bearer token.
Three message groups: calls from the app, notifications from the sidecar, and sidecar requests that wait for an answer.
Every pause point (question, approval, plan) is a real request to the UI that waits for an answer.
Claude is run with streaming input, resume, a permission prompt tool, setting sources and a disallowed tool list, all set through the SDK.
Claude is started with a plugin folder holding the bundled skill (the --plugin-dir flag).
The built-in AskUserQuestion tool is disabled and replaced by an app tool.
Environment variables for the agent: workspace path, root path, port, default branch, session id, plus workspace name, workspace id and a local flag.
The login shell is run once to capture PATH, and provider API keys are stripped from the captured environment.
Agent tools are served by an in-process MCP server in the sidecar for Claude.
Agent tools reach Codex and ACP agents through a helper process and a socket bridge.
Workspaces are git worktrees under the conductor workspaces folder, one folder per repo and place name.
Checkpoints are kept in private git refs.
The bundled git-busy-check script reports whether git is mid-operation.
The main database holds the repos, workspaces, chats and events; ours has 13 tables and 3 migrations, with one event log per chat (D006).
Conductor's separate client-side message cache database; ours has none and the UI reads the one database.
Session event outbox, one JSON file per chat.
The app downloads, verifies and updates its own copies of claude and codex in an agent-binaries folder and a bin folder, and removes old versions.
The gh program is bundled in Conductor's bin folder; ours uses the user's own gh.
The watchexec program is bundled in Conductor's bin folder for the spotlighter script; ours expects watchexec on the PATH.
Global settings file in the user's home folder; the settings registry reads it but the data model has no row for it.
Per-repo settings file inside the repo (scripts, files to copy, prompts).
Main tables: repos, workspaces, sessions, session_events and others (session_messages is dropped by D006).
Conductor writes every agent JSON line as its own row twice and reached 12 GB; ours has one log and states each store's lifetime.
Cloud workspaces in Linux sandboxes.
The UI writes every chat message and event to the database itself.
The Rust shell relays JSON-RPC lines between the UI and the sidecar.
The sidecar never writes the database; the UI is the only writer.
Step 1: the UI stores the user message first, then sends the query with its options.
Step 2: each chat has a one-at-a-time queue, and cancel skips it.
Step 3: reuse the live agent process or start one with resume.
Step 4: the first message carries a hidden instruction block, mentions and attachments.
Step 5: the start checkpoint never delays the reply; the first write waits for it.
Step 6: the query call returns when the turn starts, not when it ends.
Step 7: events are sent in batches of at most 50 events or 0.8 MB.
Step 8: the UI saves each event, then confirms; the sidecar keeps the event until confirmed.
Step 9: the turn ends on the result message, then the end checkpoint, a flush, then idle.
Chat status is only idle or working; other conditions are flags on the live state.
Follow-up queue: a user row with no sent time and a queue order; edit, reorder and delete.
Steer is a send with steering delivery, shown as pending until the agent reads it.
Agents that cannot steer do not offer steering in the UI, as in Conductor; a message sent with the default mode goes to them as a normal follow-up, and a steer asked for by name fails visibly.
Cancel stops the turn, takes the end checkpoint and drops the queued follow-ups; ours pauses the app queue instead of dropping it.
Cancel for Claude tries an in-protocol interrupt first, then SIGTERM and SIGKILL after 5 s (D015).

Ours cuts every runner's output to its first 100000 characters, so the end of a long output (often the error) is lost.

ClaudeAgentRunner tag: runner lifecycle lines such as generator restarts, results for a turn it did not start, forced settling and the executable in use.

ACP sign-in errors (code -32000) say the agent needs sign-in and list each advertised method; not retryable.
ACP errors about credits, quota, payment or billing tell the user to add credits or choose another model; not retryable.
ACP rate-limit errors (429, too many requests) tell the user to try again in a moment or choose another model; retryable.
A bare 'Internal error' from an ACP agent is replaced by the provider's last output; a missing program says the agent could not start and how to repair it.
OpenCode's MCP tool timeout is raised to at least 10 minutes in the config passed to it, so a tool that waits for a person, such as AskUserQuestion, does not time out.
Both current OpenCode major versions are supported, with their different config shapes.

In ~/.cursor/mcp.json and the workspace .cursor/mcp.json, ${env:NAME}, ${NAME} and ${NAME:-default} are filled from the environment; one invalid server is dropped with a warning naming it, the rest stay.
Remote Cursor MCP servers may carry headers, an OAuth client and a CA bundle.
A review comment file sent to the chat adds the file mentions inside it to the attached files; an unreadable comment file only logs.
Attachments are listed in two groups (paths, including those found in mentions and comment files, and file paths), each with a size label per file, or 'unknown size'.
The pull request stub .context/pull-requests/<n>.md has a heading and, when the repository is known, its GitHub URL; an existing file is kept.
A failed login-shell capture sends the app a notification with the folder, a kind (timeout, shell not found, unknown) and the message; failures are not cached, so the next call retries.
A batch also ends at any notification that changes live state or settings.

A notification above 80 percent of 1 MiB is shrunk: long fields keep a head and a tail with a note giving the original size, cut by binary search so the largest piece that fits survives; structured fields become a small stub.
checkpointer.sh output and error are each kept up to 64 KiB for the log line.
A sign-in returns a login id, a login URL, a user code and a verification URL; later calls finish or cancel it.

Model entries carry what the picker shows: short label, new badge, wire name, alias, status (picker, gated, hidden, deprecated), provider family, effort axis label and level labels, default effort and model, fork model, fast-mode default, thinking budgets, live effort switch, the minimum agent version and the agents it fits.
A goal carries an objective, a status and a token budget; a message starting with /goal (pause, resume, clear, or an objective) becomes the matching call.
A live-state update can carry only the pending steers.
Codex usage carries named rate limits with a primary and a secondary window (used percent, window length, reset time) and token counts with the context window.

zLiveState carries autoApproveEdits (packages/protocol/src/live-state.ts); SessionManager.setAutoApproveEdits and the allow_edits_for_session answer publish it through LiveStateStore, so the composer's auto-accept chip (ModeChips) reads liveStates[sessionId]?.autoApproveEdits instead of its local copy (AGENT-04) (moved from COMP-03 by the slice 2 step 1 audit).

Start the app tools bridge at sidecar startup again (removed in slice 2 step 1 because AppToolsBridge.start() was a placeholder that stopped the sidecar from starting), and stop calling bridge.stop() at shutdown until the bridge exists.
Fill the saved terminal history in core/services/terminals.ts (created but never filled), so a terminal shows its earlier screen after a reload; PLAT-08 owns the Rust side.

Tauri.ts attachment wiring: `createTauriAttachments.materialize`/`resizeImage` still call `notImplemented("PLAT-33")`, so the Rust commands and the "A command materializes dropped or pasted attachments" / "added from a file picker, drag and drop or paste" items are reachable only from Rust tests
5 MB image refusal: the Rust limit is 4.5 MiB after resize; refusing images over 5 MB and showing the "Image too large" banner/message belong to the composer
Help > Diagnostics menu item: needs `app.openDiagnostics` in the command registry and a handler
Debug menu item handler: `app.openDebugTools` has no command-runner handler; it should call `platform.window.toggleInspector()`
Menu accelerators and menu clicks in the live app: `createTauriMenu.setShortcuts` and `onCommand` still call `notImplemented("PLAT-33")`

The Environment page's variables reach a running agent: SET-04 adds them to the agent launch that SIDE-21 builds (global variables, then the repository's of the same name), and an idle agent restarts with resume when they change.
The managed agent copy joins the program order (Settings path, managed copy, then PATH) when PLAT-28 installs it; until then the order is Settings path, then PATH.

The desktop composition root (core/container.ts) passes launchFor to SessionsService and ChatTitlesService, built from the saved settings: program paths, provider and base URL, and provider keys from the Keychain. Accepted by a test over createTestContainer that sends one message and sees the launch in the sidecar request, with no chat_launch_missing (D054).

After a revert the agent forgets the reverted turns: revertTo asks the sidecar to resetAgent, and the chat's next send resumes the agent at the chosen turn with resume.atNativeMessageId. Until then the agent keeps them in memory although the chat hides them (moved by the s2-2 core-1 audit).
Linear requests go through Platform.http (http_fetch) instead of curl (moved from PLAT-30 by the slice 2 step 2 audit).
Agent and helper program downloads go through Platform.http.download with a SHA-256 and cancel (moved from PLAT-30 by the slice 2 step 2 audit).
